candidate.answerReason: Factoring gives (2x+3)(2x−10)=0, with roots −3/2 and 5. Their sum is 7/2.

methods.label: Use the shared factor
methods.explanation:
Both terms contain \(2x+3\), so factoring out that expression reveals the roots directly:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(2x+3)(x-4)+(2x+3)(x-6)\\
&\qquad=(2x+3)\bigl((x-4)+(x-6)\bigr)\\
&\qquad=(2x+3)(2x-10).
\end{aligned}
\]
A product is zero exactly when at least one factor is zero. Thus all the roots are given by
\[
2x+3=0\quad\text{or}\quad2x-10=0,
\]
so \(x=-\frac32\) or \(x=5\). Their sum is
\[
-\frac32+5=\boxed{\frac72},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
